title: SKU rotation & queue smoothing (Fulfillment lanes)
content:
Purpose:
  Lightweight planning sheet to manage interregional SKU rotation, order queue smoothing, and fulfillment lanes when spot/commit mixes shift. Designed for quick ops decisions during 8–12 week procurement horizons.

Scope and assumptions:
  - Regions covered: us-west, us-east, eu-west, apac-sg
  - SKUs tracked: 80GB-H100, 80GB-A100, 40GB-H100, 48GB-GPU-e (proxy for future gen)
  - Burn rate = avg usable hours/day * daily requests (normalized) -> converted to 'effective GPU-days'
  - Lead times = supplier quoted calendar days (inc customs) + 7 days contingency for logistics
  - Safety buffer policy: dynamic (target percentile of historical supply variance), default 18% of on-hand in prod regions

Quick summary (1-line):
  Current forecast shows a 6–9 week elevated burn in eu-west due to new Dedicated beta; recommend 2 staggered micro-orders of 80GB-H100 directed to eu-west and a temporary intra-region rotation from us-west (reallocate 6 units for 4 weeks).

Table (columns):
  SKU | Region | On-hand units | Committed (dedicated) | Avg daily burn | Open ordered units | Supplier ETA | ETA slack (days) | Safety buffer units | Recommended action

  80GB-H100 | us-west | 72 | 8 | 1.4 | 12 | 2026-03-28 | 10 | 13 | hold reassign 6 -> eu-west for 28 days; speed up customs for open order GH-498
  80GB-H100 | eu-west | 18 | 14 | 2.3 | 6 | 2026-04-15 | 18 | 5 | place micro-order (4 units) with expedited freight; rotate 6 from us-west
  80GB-A100 | us-east | 54 | 6 | 0.9 | 0 | 2026-06-04 | 60 | 10 | keep pipeline; evaluate quantization to reduce burn
  40GB-H100 | apac-sg | 24 | 2 | 0.6 | 8 | 2026-03-22 | 6 | 6 | accept arrival; distribute 4 -> apac-edge pool, keep 4 for testing
  48GB-GPU-e | us-west | 0 | 0 | 0.0 | 16 | 2026-04-10 | 7 | 3 | staggered inbound: 8 -> us-west prod, 8 -> test/bench; delay activation until canary complete

Operational rules embedded in sheet:
  - Queue smoothing: split any large order > 12 units into at least 2 shipments spaced 14 days apart unless SLA requires immediate fulfillment.
  - Rotation window: reassignable units must have >21 days remaining on warranty/reservation and not be locked by customer tenancy.
  - Fallback lane: if ETA slack <= 10 days and on-hand < (committed + safety buffer) => auto-escalate to procurement on-call and/or invoke secondary supplier.

Decision log snippets (recent):
  - 2026-01-30: Approved micro-order strategy for eu-west to avoid bulk spot exposure (ticket JIRA:PROC-3910).
  - 2026-02-05: SRE requested temporary rotation of 6 units from us-west to eu-west for Dedicated beta; ops noted potential 7-day customs delta.
  - 2026-02-12: Held larger A100 tranche to evaluate pricing hedge; finance flagged 30% unit price variance if split across tranches.

Open action items (short):
  - @Marco: confirm expedited freight cost estimate for 4x 80GB-H100 (due 2026-02-18).
  - @Leah: validate which instances are eligible for rotation without tenant migration (due 2026-02-16).
  - @Priya: update supplier ETA gap analysis with customs runtime for eu ports (due 2026-02-20).

Scenario simulation snippets (for runbook):
  - Scenario A (late supplier, +21 days): move to secondary supplier lane; pre-approve 4 units from spot reserve; increase safety buffer by 8% across eu-west for next 6 weeks.
  - Scenario B (early arrival, -7 days): accelerate onboarding runbook; prioritize canary + 25% of new units to Dedicated; remaining to reduce burn in us-west by 10%.
  - Scenario C (surge demand in apac): trigger cross-region borrow from us-east with 5-day airlift; require exec approval if >10 units.

Notes on metrics used in sheet (how to interpret):
  - "Avg daily burn" is computed from 28-day trailing median of allocation hours and normalized to units/day (approx usable GPU-days).
  - "ETA slack" = (Supplier ETA date - projected depletion date) in calendar days. Negative -> immediate shortage risk.

References & links:
  - Procurement playbook (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Procurement+Guidelines
  - Queue smoothing RFC: GH:repo/infra/pulls/498 (mentioned in linked_artifacts)
  - Slack thread #procurement-ops: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C12345ABC

Appendix (quick formulas):
  - projected_depletion_date = today + (on-hand - safety_buffer + open_order_inbound_adjustment) / avg_daily_burn
  - recommended_tranche_count = ceil(open_quantity / 12) unless cost penalty override

Quick heuristics for on-call procurement:
  - If projected_depletion_date <= today + 10 days for any prod region, escalate.
  - Prefer micro-orders to large bulks when lead-time uncertainty > 30%.
  - Use rotation before new procurement when rotation cost (reassign + freight) < 1.2x unit price spread.

This sheet is intentionally compact to be copy-pasted into weekly ops emails. For full modelling, see 'fleet-supply-simulator' (internal notebook) and link GH:repo/infra#467.
